question: What is the main goal of disaster mitigation?

options.A: To completely eliminate all natural hazards on earth
options.B: To manage patients only after a disaster has occurred
options.C: To reduce the severity and impact of potential disasters
options.D: To provide immediate funding for post-disaster recovery

explanation: You've got this! Mitigation is all about lessening the damage from hazards that we cannot completely stop. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h1)

question: Which of these is a primary prevention action in a community?

options.A: Rebuilding a hospital that was destroyed by an earthquake
options.B: Building a strong embankment to stop seasonal river flooding
options.C: Treating injured victims at a temporary field clinic
options.D: Providing counseling for survivors after a major fire outbreak

explanation: Great job thinking ahead! Primary prevention stops the hazard from causing harm before it even happens. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h1)

question: What does a risk assessment mainly look at?

options.A: The speed at which emergency vehicles can travel
options.B: The exact budget needed to rebuild a damaged clinic
options.C: The likelihood of a hazard and population vulnerability
options.D: The personal medical history of disaster survivors

explanation: Spot on! Risk assessment combines how likely an event is with how exposed and vulnerable the people are. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h2)

question: A community has strong local leadership and plenty of food supplies even though droughts happen often. What do we call these strengths?
explanation: Well done! Capacities are simply the strengths and resources a community uses to stand strong against disasters. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h2)

question: Which of these is an example of structural mitigation in a hospital?

options.A: Teaching community members how to wash their hands
options.B: Bolting heavy oxygen tanks securely to the wall
options.C: Writing a new policy on emergency communication
options.D: Conducting a fire drill for the nursing staff

explanation: You nailed it! Structural mitigation involves making physical changes to buildings or equipment to keep people safe. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h3)

question: A clinic is in an area that floods every rainy season. What is the best structural safety step for them?

options.A: Issuing warning pamphlets to patients in the waiting room
options.B: Training nurses on how to swim in fast-moving water
options.C: Buying extra bandages and IV fluids for the pharmacy
options.D: Moving the emergency backup generators to an upper floor

explanation: Brilliant! Elevating power systems protects them from floodwaters so the clinic can keep running. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h3)

question: Which activity is an example of non-structural disaster mitigation?

options.A: Installing steel reinforcement pillars in a hospital ward
options.C: Building a high concrete wall around a reservoir
options.D: Enforcing strict zoning laws to stop building in floodplains

explanation: That's right! Laws and policies are non-structural measures that guide us away from dangerous areas without physical building changes. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h4)

question: Why is land-use planning so helpful for disaster prevention?

options.A: It physically reinforces old buildings against strong winds
options.B: It provides immediate medical care to disaster survivors
options.C: It replaces the need for community disaster education
options.D: It prevents people from settling in naturally hazardous zones

explanation: Spot on! Good land-use planning keeps people and important buildings safely away from high-risk spots. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h4)

question: When a local disaster strikes, who is almost always the very first responder?
explanation: You got it! Neighbors and local residents are already right there to help before official rescue teams arrive. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h5)

question: What is the main benefit of regular disaster drills in a community?

options.A: It completely stops natural disasters from happening
options.B: It reduces panic and builds muscle memory for safe evacuation
options.C: It guarantees that no property damage will ever occur
options.D: It replaces the need for building structural flood walls

explanation: Well done! Practice makes calm; drills help people respond automatically and safely during real emergencies. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h5)

question: How can clinical nurses take part in disaster prevention?

options.A: Managing the national budget for emergency services
options.B: Educating patients on protecting vital medicines during power cuts
options.C: Passing national laws that restrict building near riverbanks
options.D: Designing heavy structural blueprints for new hospitals

explanation: Fantastic! Nurses help patients prepare by teaching them how to manage their health when emergencies happen. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h6)

question: How do nurses help make hospitals safer against disasters?

options.A: By funding the construction of new earthquake-proof walls
options.B: By purchasing emergency generators with personal funds
options.C: By writing national environmental zoning policies
options.D: By serving on disaster committees and pointing out safety hazards

explanation: Spot on! Nurses use their daily ward experience to help planners catch and fix safety risks early. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h6)

question: What is the main job of agencies like NEMA and SEMA in Nigeria?

options.A: To manage hospital nursing shifts and patient charts
options.B: To construct residential housing in safe urban zones
options.C: To coordinate emergency management, warnings, and disaster response
options.D: To manufacture pharmaceutical drugs for public clinics

explanation: You got it! These agencies bring together planning, warnings, and relief efforts across the country. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h7)

question: Why do different agencies need to work together during a disaster response?

options.A: It gives nurses the authority to write new national laws
options.B: It replaces the need for community education and local drills
options.C: It guarantees that natural hazards will completely miss the country
options.D: It ensures that different groups do not duplicate efforts and waste resources

explanation: Brilliant! Sharing information and working hand-in-hand prevents confusion and keeps help running smoothly. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h7)
